subject: geography
title: Settlement Hierarchy
welcome_lead: From tiny hamlets to giant cities — settlements come in a hierarchy. Climb the ladder and discover each level!
meta_desc: KS3 Geography adventure on settlement hierarchy from hamlet to megacity.
final_note: Excellent! You now understand the settlement hierarchy.

concepts.def: Very small settlement, just a few houses.
Small rural settlement with basic services.
Larger settlement with shops and services.
Big settlement, often with a cathedral or charter.
Many cities merged into one huge area.
Things people need: shops, schools, hospitals.

walkthroughs.body_html: From smallest to biggest: hamlet → village → town → city → conurbation → megacity. Each level has more people and more services.
A hamlet may have nothing. A village has a shop and pub. A city has hospitals, universities and big shops. Higher up the hierarchy, more services.
A hamlet in Yorkshire, a village in Devon, a town like Reading, a city like Birmingham, a conurbation like Greater Manchester.

options: Merged cities forming a huge area
